header.tag_why: The signer, the COO who owned stores, was comparing how returns, tills and a 120-store rollout would work on one platform, and we only described that while Adyen (per Raj) showed up with a retail rollout team and one contract.

evidence.excerpt: Returns. Last holiday season. Buy online, return in store.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: The store couldn't see the online order, so staff were refunding to gift cards or telling people to mail it back.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: they'd just launched a loyalty program that was supposed to work everywhere and didn't, because store and web were two different customer records.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: Their COO, Angela, apparently stood in a store on December 27th watching the returns queue.
evidence.label: opinion

trigger.insight: The evaluation started as a store operations problem: online orders that couldn't be returned at the till, and a loyalty program broken by split customer records. The story the customer tells about it centers on the COO, not the CTO. Our pitch then led with web checkout, the one area that wasn't hurting. We answered a question the customer wasn't asking.
trigger.messaging: For retailers, open with returning an online order at a store till and one customer record across channels, not M1's global-currency line or web checkout.

evidence.excerpt: The CTO, Raj. He ran the RFP, he was my contact the whole way.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: Angela.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: ...Probably Angela. Raj wanted us. I think. He told me he did.
evidence.label: opinion

evidence.excerpt: Once. The kickoff.
evidence.label: fact

decider.insight: Tom named the person who ran the process as the decider. The person who signed was the COO, whose team asked for the stores workshop and whom Tom met only once. Raj's support rests only on Raj's word, and the 'we were ahead' signal came from him too. We were scoring ourselves against the wrong person's criteria.
decider.messaging: Retail messaging must speak to the COO and store-ops buyer (accountability, rollout, the tills), not only to the CTO who runs the RFP.

evidence.excerpt: This is secondhand. Raj told me afterwards.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: they came in with a retail team, people who'd done store rollouts, and they talked about one platform for the tills and the website, on one contract.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: After, it was stores. What happens when the store wifi drops. How do you roll out 120 stores. Who shows up when a till goes down on a Saturday.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: Raj forwarded me a list of 14 questions and 11 of them were about stores.
evidence.label: fact

competitor.insight: After the customer met Adyen, the evaluation moved off the web, where we led, and onto stores: 11 of the 14 follow-up questions were about stores. Per Raj, Adyen pitched people with rollout experience, one contract and retailers Angela knew. That matches Angela's fear of 'two vendors pointing at each other.' Tom saw none of this directly and heard about it only after the decision.
competitor.messaging: Match the store-side questions with concrete answers (offline till behavior, rollout sequencing for many stores, weekend till coverage) before a competitor sets that agenda.

evidence.excerpt: Reaction: the online checkout demo. Their ecommerce lead loved it.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: Online and in-store on one platform, the line between them has pretty much disappeared.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: that's a diagram.
evidence.label: quote
evidence.speaker: Bev

evidence.excerpt: I described it.
evidence.label: fact

message.insight: The M2 checkout demo won over someone who didn't decide. The M3 unified-commerce claim was dismissed by store ops as 'a diagram.' When Bev asked for the return step by step at the till, we described it instead of showing it. M3 is an assertion with no proof, and to an operations buyer a claim with no demo reads as a gap.
message.messaging: Replace M3's slide line with a recorded step-by-step return of an online order at a till, and lead with it in retail decks.

evidence.excerpt: When Bev asked who does the installs, I said we'd bring in a partner. She wrote something down and didn't ask another question.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: I knew on the drive home.
evidence.label: opinion

evidence.excerpt: Right before that, honestly, we were ahead. Raj said so. We'd won the web side.
evidence.label: opinion

evidence.excerpt: They had six people from store operations. Nobody on our side had run a store rollout.
evidence.label: fact

decided.insight: The turning point was the store ops workshop, which Angela's team requested. There, the answer that 'a partner' does installs introduced exactly the second vendor Angela didn't want. Being 'ahead' was a web-only lead reported by the CTO, while the signer's team was judging stores. We sent a two-person web-strength team to face six store-ops people.
decided.messaging: State plainly who owns installs, rollout and till outages end to end; if a partner is involved, message single accountability explicitly, never 'we'd bring in a partner.'

evidence.excerpt: can I talk to them?
evidence.label: quote
evidence.speaker: Angela

evidence.excerpt: we couldn't set up a call in time.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: Then a rollout plan. Dates, who installs, what happens to the old tills.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: They wanted to watch an online order get returned at a store till, live. We described it. We never showed it.
evidence.label: fact

gaps.insight: The customer asked for three things: a retailer they could call, a rollout plan, and a live return at a till. Tom lists all three among what we couldn't show. Every one is proof, not features. M8's 'see our customer stories' failed in practice: the decider wanted a phone call, not a case study. Whether we can actually do the live return is not established; we only know it was never shown.
gaps.messaging: Back M3 and M8 with a callable retail reference on standby, a template multi-store rollout plan, and a live online-to-till return demo.

evidence.excerpt: One system for the tills and the website.
evidence.label: quote
evidence.speaker: Bev

evidence.excerpt: I don't want two vendors pointing at each other.
evidence.label: quote
evidence.speaker: Angela

evidence.excerpt: one customer, one basket.
evidence.label: quote
evidence.speaker: Angela

evidence.excerpt: We kept saying 'in-person payments' and 'point of sale.' They said 'the tills.'
evidence.label: fact

language.insight: The customer talked about operations and accountability: tills, one system, one customer, one basket, and no finger-pointing vendors. We talked in category jargon: unified commerce, in-person payments, point of sale. Angela's 'two vendors' line is the clearest statement of the deciding criterion in the whole interview, and our partner-install answer collided with it directly.
language.messaging: Rewrite M3 in their words, e.g. one system for the tills and the website, one customer, one basket, one vendor accountable, and drop 'unified commerce' and 'point of sale' with retail buyers.

gaps.question: What exactly did Tom say when Bev asked how a return works at the till, and how did she react?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Tom: walk through what you described to Bev step by step, and what she said or did afterwards.

gaps.question: Who made the final call, and how do you know?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Tom: what evidence beyond Raj's word shows Raj supported us, and did Raj say why Angela chose Adyen? If possible, ask Raj directly what Angela weighed.

gaps.question: What was the customer using before (incumbent tills and web payments)?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Tom: what did they run on the tills and the website before, and what were they planning to do with the old tills?

gaps.question: Did Angela ever see our pitch beyond the kickoff, and what did she hear from us about stores?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Tom: did Angela attend the store ops workshop or receive any material from us after kickoff?

gaps.question: Can we actually demonstrate an online order returned at a store till, and why was it not shown?
gaps.follow_up: Ask the solutions engineer: is this demo feasible today, and what blocked showing it to Marlowe & Finch?

gaps.question: Why couldn't we set up a reference call in time?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Tom and the customer reference team: which retail references exist with stores and online, and how long a call takes to arrange.

close.rep_takeaway: Being ahead with your contact is not being ahead with the signer. When the stores team asked for their own workshop, that was the signal that the decision had moved to the COO. That's the moment to get in front of her and bring people who have done store rollouts, a live till demo and a callable retailer. Describing something to an operations buyer who asked to see it counts as a no.
